place_name_en: Great Hall of the People Chongqing

sources.title: Chongqing Great Hall of People, Chongqing People's Auditorium
sources.content:
The Chongqing Great Hall of the People, also called the Chongqing People's Auditorium, serves as a large hall for political meetings and cultural events and stands as an architectural landmark in central Chongqing.

Address: Renmin Road, Yuzhong District, Chongqing

Transportation:
Metro Line 10 to Dahuitang Station, Exit 1
Metro Line 2 to Zengjiayan Station, Exit 3
Bus routes 145, 152, and 181 to Dahuitang Station

Hours & Entry:
Operating Hours: 8:30 AM - 5:00 PM
Entry Fee: Approximately 10 CNY for interior visits

Historical Background: Construction began in June 1951 and completed in April 1954. Builders faced significant challenges, employing the 'method of pilling' with more than 35000 board step-stone due to limited heavy equipment availability.

Architecture: The structure stands 65 meters tall with five stories, accommodating 4,206 people. The design incorporates architectural features of the Ming and Qing dynasties with traditional central axis symmetry and double-eave colonnades.

Viewing Recommendations:
Outdoor Spots: Ma'an Mountain Hall Lane offers panoramic architectural views; People Square directly faces the Hall's full facade; Three Gorges Museum steps provide elevated frontal angles.
Night Viewing: 8:00 PM - 9:30 PM illumination creates a golden appearance.

Nearby Attractions: Three Gorges Museum (3-minute walk), Zhongshan Fourth Road (10-minute walk), Crown Escalator at Two-Road-Mouth, Liziba Monorail-Through-Building, E'ling Park.

sources.title: Great Hall of the People, Chongqing: The Ethnic Building Complex
sources.content:
The Great Hall of the People in Chongqing represents a significant architectural achievement from China's early post-1949 period. Originally called the Southwest Administrative Committee Grand Auditorium, it received its current name in 1956. Construction spanned from 1951 to 1954, making it one of the city's important landmark buildings that achieved international recognition when ranked highly by the Royal Institute of British Architects in 1987.

Design Philosophy: The structure draws heavily from Ming and Qing dynasty palace aesthetics. Its layout employs traditional axial symmetry that creates a harmonious and striking structural balance. The central dome's golden apex references Beijing's Temple of Heaven.

Key Components:
Archway: Features four columns and three spans, showcasing typical Ming and Qing dynasty architectural styles
Main Hall: Requires ascending 128 steps across three levels
Wings: Include colonnaded sloped roofs with four corner towers
Central Tower: Miniature version of Beijing's Tiananmen

Hours & Admission: Opens 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM; entrance costs 10 yuan (online reservation required)
Location: No. 173, Renmin Road, Yuzhong District
Transit: Metro Line 2, Zengjiayan Station

People's Square: Sprawls across approximately 240,000 square meters, featuring granite paving, musical fountains, and housing hundreds of pigeons for public enjoyment.

Three Gorges Antique City: Adjacent marketplace specializing in calligraphy, ceramics, jewelry, and traditional crafts.

sources.title: Tips for Visiting Great Hall of the People in Chongqing - CITS
sources.content:
The Chongqing Great Hall of the People was built in June 1951 and finished in April 1954 with a total height of 65 meters, accommodating an audience of 4,206 people. Built in the 1950s, it is an exquisite imitation of ancient ethnic buildings with a dome that imitates the Temple of Heaven, representing the roundness of the sky.

Best Times to Visit: Early morning or late afternoon offer the best lighting and fewer crowds, with weekdays being quieter than weekends.

Entrance Fees & Access: There is an entrance fee of RMB 8 per person.

Photography: The exterior architecture, particularly the dome inspired by the Temple of Heaven, is a prime subject. The area around the People's Assembly Hall is well-guarded by police, making it a safe place to take photos in the evening.

Getting There: You can reach it easily by metro - Linjiangmen Station on Line 1 is the closest stop, about a 10-minute walk away.

More than 260,000 pieces of gold have been decorated on the top part inside the hall, which cost 10 RMB per piece and make the building dazzlingly brilliant.

Recommended visit duration: About 1-2 hours for a thorough visit.

sources.title: Chongqing's Great Hall of the People - In Photos - Journey Rambler
sources.content:
The Great Hall of the People was perhaps one of the more memorable places visitors can experience when in Chongqing, with the People's Auditorium being serious, somber, yet still rich in history and culture. The entrance ticket is 10 RMB per person and well worth it if you want to get a closer look at the architectural marvel.

If time allows, visitors can enter the Hall to admire its impressive dome, ornate decorations, and rows of signature red seats, with the interior exuding a strong historical atmosphere and being worth experiencing for its cultural significance.

The Great Hall of the People ranks in the top 10 of classical Asian architecture of the 20th century and the Classic Chinese Centennial Building of the 20th century. Construction began in 1951 and was completed in 1954, located at People's Square in Yuzhong District.

The Ming and Qing Dynasty architecture and a mix of soviet architecture make the Great Hall look at once both grand and like a temple.

sources.title: People's Assembly Hall (2026) - Chongqing - Tripadvisor
sources.content: People's Assembly Hall visitor reviews from Tripadvisor. Located in central Chongqing, the Great Hall is a must-see architectural landmark. Visitors recommend visiting both the exterior and interior, with the dome being particularly impressive. The nearby People's Square offers great photo opportunities. Best visited in combination with the Three Gorges Museum which is just across the square. The building is especially beautiful when illuminated at night. Getting there by metro is convenient via Line 2 to Daxigou Station, then walk about 15 minutes.

sources.title: 重庆市人民大礼堂_百度百科
sources.content:
重庆市人民大礼堂位于渝中区人民路173号，于1951年6月破土兴建，1954年4月竣工。它是一座仿古民族建筑群，被誉为重庆十大文化符号之一，也是中国传统宫殿建筑风格与西方建筑大跨度结构的结合典范。

景点级别：AAAA级
门票价格：10元/人
开放时间：8:00-18:00（17:30停止入场）
占地面积：6.6万平方米

建设沿革：1951年春，刘伯承、邓小平、贺龙等领导决定筹建大礼堂。1951年6月张家德设计方案被采纳。1954年4月竣工交付使用。1956年改名为重庆市人民大礼堂。1997年重庆直辖，拆除围墙建设人民广场。

结构规模：礼堂建筑高65米，大厅净空高55米，内径46.33米，圆形大厅四周环绕四层挑楼，可容纳3400余人。大礼堂由中心礼堂和南、北、东楼四大部分组成。

设计特色：仿明、清的宫殿形式，采用轴向对称的传统手法。主体穹庶金顶参照北京天坛祈年殿设计。中间的半圆形球壳顶架为双层钢架结构。牌坊整体以橘红和红色为主色调，上覆碧绿琉璃瓦。

文物保护：2013年5月被列入第七批全国重点文物保护单位。2016年9月入选首批中国20世纪建筑遗产名录。

荣誉：1987年在英国皇家建筑学会《比较建筑史》中位列第二。2002年评定为国家AAAA级旅游景区。被评为亚洲二十世纪十大经典建筑。

交通：轨道交通2号线大溪沟站步行约930米；10号线大礼堂站步行740米。公交112、145、152、181等多条线路。

sources.title: 人民大礼堂_重庆市人民政府网
sources.content: 重庆市人民大礼堂是重庆市的标志性建筑之一，位于渝中区人民路。始建于1951年，1954年竣工。大礼堂是一座仿古民族建筑群，融合了中国传统宫殿建筑风格与西方建筑的大跨度结构。建筑高65米，可容纳4206人。大礼堂与人民广场、三峡博物馆形成三位一体的城市标志建筑群，是重庆最具代表性的地标景点之一。
